note: quince#306, the DIAGNOSIS half. r4 observed a newly declared issue emitting a comment event for a comment SEVEN HOURS OLD, while a second issue declared 70 minutes later baselined silently — two behaviours, same tool, same session, and it could not settle which was the defect. Neither is. `issue-first-observation` fires on `$o == null`: NOT IN THE PREVIOUS OBSERVATION. Declaring an issue is not what baselines it — being unseen is. Here #83 is already in the set as `via=referenced`, because the session's own open PR names it (quince#80 half two watches those automatically, with no declaration). Declaring it only changes `via=`, so the diff runs as it always has and the comment that accrued since the last observation is emitted — correctly, and that is how r4 found an architect ruling it had missed. The age of the comment is IRRELEVANT and is the thing that made this look wrong: what the tool compares is the stored observation, so a state file that is seven hours stale reports seven hours of accrual on its next tick. Pair with issue306-a-genuinely-new-issue-baselines-however-old-its-comments.json — that one holds the comment age fixed and changes only whether the issue was already there, which is the single variable this whole report turns on.
